title: Dangling Pointers
concept: Holding onto a receipt (pointer) for returned memory -- and then causing an accident

steps.title: Including stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Standard I/O header.

This lesson covers the dangling pointer problem -- a pointer that still references freed memory.

steps.title: Including stdlib.h header
steps.explanation: This header is needed to use `malloc`/`free`.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created. We will follow the allocate -> free -> safe cleanup flow.

steps.title: Allocating heap memory
steps.explanation: We allocate space for one integer on the heap and store the address in pointer `p`.

steps.title: Storing a value in heap memory
steps.explanation: `*p = 10;` completes initialization of the heap value.

steps.title: Freeing memory and creating a dangling pointer
steps.explanation:
After `free(p)`, the heap block is freed but the value of `p` remains unchanged, leaving it in a dangling state.

Dereferencing this pointer causes Undefined Behavior.

steps.title: Preventing dangling pointers (the fix)
steps.explanation:
`p = NULL;` invalidates the pointer to reduce the risk of reuse.

Setting to NULL immediately after freeing is the most basic defensive habit.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
The program ends with `return 0;`.

Key point: After free, immediately set the pointer to NULL.

quiz.question: What is a Dangling Pointer?
options: A pointer that still points to freed (invalid) memory
quiz.explanation:
"Dangling" means hanging loosely.
It refers to a pointer that has lost its valid destination.

misconceptions.wrong: After free(p), p automatically becomes NULL
misconceptions.why: Manually writing `p = NULL;` is both good manners and a survival skill for C programmers.

keyTakeaway: After `free`, tear up the receipt (`p`) too -- set it to `NULL`.
